rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads alif-lam-mim as “I am Allah, the All-Knowing”; Elmalılı approves it as symbolic meaning and the culmination of reflection on the address.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden mervî olan vücûh içinde

rows.speaker: Ebû Bekir
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reports that every book has a secret of God, and the Quran’s secret is its sūra openings.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’den mervî olan

rows.speaker: Alî
rows.claim: Ali reports that every book has a kernel, and the kernel of this Book is the alphabet letters.
rows.anchor: diye Hazret-i Alî’den mervî olan

rows.speaker: Alî
rows.claim: Ali reports that the disjoint letters Ḥā Mīm ʿAyn Sīn Qāf and Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād are divine names; Elmalılı treats this as aligned with the other reports.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Alî’den mervî olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because these reported meanings encompass one another, Elmalılı classifies the sūra initials among the mutashābihāt.
rows.anchor: Ve hepsine şâmil olduğu için mukatta‘ât-ı süver müteşabihâttandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutashābihāt are not meaningless or wholly obscure; their many meanings and comprehensive truths exceed human capacity, making a determinate intent seem impossible.
rows.anchor: Müteşabihât mânasız ve mühmel değil, kesret-i me‘ânîden dolayı muayyen bir murad ta‘yîni mümkin görünmeyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutashābih expression can contain the full range of rhetorical modes, from literal and figurative to explicit, allusive, illustrative, verified, apparent, and hidden.
rows.anchor: hakikat, mecaz, sarih, kinaye, temsil, tahkik, zâhir, hafî gibi vücûh-i beyânın mecmû‘unu hâvîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity cannot bear comprehensive communication of all divine knowledge, and prophetic knowledge is not equal to God's; Elmalılı cites the prayer for increased knowledge.
rows.anchor: Ulûm-i enbiyâ bile ilmullâha müsâvi olamaz وَقُلْ رَبِّ زِدْن۪ي عِلْماً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Opening with a mysterious, wonder-provoking address powerfully captures attention and creates an eloquent force of attraction at the beginning of guidance.
rows.anchor: Kur’ân’ın başında irşad ve hidâyetin bidâyetinde böyle hayret-engiz bir teblîğin beliğ bir kuvve-i teshîriyesi vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers unable to answer the Quran urged listeners to make noise over its recitation so they might overpower it.
rows.anchor: küffâr لاَ تَسْمَعُوا لِهٰذَا الْقُرْاٰنِ وَالْغَوْا ف۪يهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَغْلِبُونَ derler

rows.speaker: İbn Ravk ve Kutrub
rows.claim: Rāzī and other tafsirs report from Ibn Ravq and Qutrub that the initials’ startling sound drew disbelievers’ attention, stopped their noise, and let them benefit from the Quran; Elmalılı calls this a cause of revelation.
rows.anchor: Râzî vesâire tefsirlerinde İbn Ravk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonder-opening need not begin al-Fātiḥa: awareness precedes wonder, while the Quran’s first aim is knowledge and guidance; before its clear monotheism, the device could harm.
rows.anchor: ilk şuur, hayretten mukaddemdir ve Kur’ân’ın gayesi de evvelen ve bizzat ilim ve hidâyete müteveccihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initials can also designate their sūra by name; a clear meaning does not prevent a phrase from naming a sūra.
rows.anchor: bu mukatta‘âtın bulundukları sûreye dahi bir isim gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken as letter names being enumerated, alif-lām-mīm have no iʿrāb, like enumerated singulars or an initial sentence.
rows.anchor: isimleri evvelâ zâhirleri vechile ta‘dâd mevki‘inde bulunduklarından i‘râbları yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses include subject and predicate, an omitted subject’s predicate, an object of an omitted command or oath, or a subject with “that is the Book” as predicate; accusative best attracts attention and strengthens an oath sense, but is not universal.
rows.anchor: nasb i‘râbı işbu hurûfa nazar-ı dikkati celb etmek nokta-i nazarından eblağdır ve bunda ma‘nâ-yı kasem daha kuvvetlidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif-lām signals the definite article, while mīm replaces lām as the article in some Arabic dialects; the cited prophetic wording means fasting while travelling is not piety.
rows.anchor: “mîm” dahi lügat-ı Arab’ın bazısında “lâm” yerine harf-i ta‘rîftir. أَمِنَ امْبِرِّ امْصِیَامُ فِي امْسَفَرِ suâline karşı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letters evoke particular, familiar sounds rather than generic alphabet sounds; the opening address is directed first and foremost to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: bu seslerin ‘ale’l-ıtlâk hurûf-i hecâ sesleri değil bir garâbet-i bedî‘a içinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı identifies the initials with extraordinary revelation sounds ringing in Muhammad’s hearing and fixing the Quran’s forms and meanings in his heart; only the Prophet knows their distinctive qualities.
rows.anchor: bu sesler Kur’an nâzil olurken sem‘-i Muhammedîde bir hususiyet ile çınlayan ve suver u me‘ânîsini kalb-i risaletpenâhîlerine takrîr u tesbît eden vahiy sesleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He glosses “Alif Lām Mīm” as the extraordinary sounds Muhammad immediately recognizes as revelation, whose audible forms and meanings begin to appear uniquely to him.
rows.anchor: Allahu a‘lem, yâ Muhammed! “Elif Lâm Mîm” denilince

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the extraordinary sounds and their marvelous ordering, revealed by God to the Prophet’s heart: the Quran’s miraculous wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: işte o sesler ve o seslere verilen nizâm-ı bedî‘ile sana ve senin kalbine min-tarafillah inzal edilmekte bulunan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kitāb is the complete, singular Book worthy of that title, the proof of truth and rulings, or the majestic, weighty divine speech promised in 73:5.
rows.anchor: tam kitap, yegâne “kitap” ıtlâkına sezâ olan o burhân-ı hakk u ahkâm, yahut اِنَّا سَنُلْق۪ي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلاً ثَق۪يلَاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among Muslims, “the Book” comes to mean the Quran alone; prophetic reports are customarily called Sunna rather than “Book.”
rows.anchor: Müslümanlar beyninde “kitap” denilince ancak Kur’an anlaşılır. Hatta ehâdîs-i nebeviyeye bile “kitap” denilmez de “sünnet” tâbir olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quranic Book is what was revealed to Muhammad, each sūra of which is inimitable, transmitted to us by mass transmission, written in muṣḥafs, and named as a whole or in part.
rows.anchor: Peygamberimiz Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Efendimiz’e inzal edilmiş olup her bir sûresi i‘câz ifade eden ve ondan bize tevâtüren menkul

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of kitāb is ketb/kitābet, joining or collecting letters in writing; customary usage then extends it from writing to what is written.
rows.anchor: asl-ı lügatta “ketb” ve “kitabet” gibi bir zamm u cem‘mânasını mutazammın olarak, hurûfu birbirine zammetmek, yani yazmak mânasına masdar iken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Book” can refer to a written collection or to the verbal expression conveyed by writing; in either case, its intended meaning is understood through the wording.
rows.anchor: Evvelkinde “kitap” bir yere yazılmış olan yazı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A book or Quran cannot consist of meaning alone: meaning is neither read nor written, so the reality of the Book comprises wording that signifies meaning, or wording and meaning together.
rows.anchor: Hakīkat-i kitâb, o mânaya dâll olan nazm ve nihâyet nazm ve mâna mecmû‘udur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wording helps thinkers grasp and distinguish meaning; removing linguistic forms would leave no firmness in ideas, so a Quran or book consisting only of meaning is inconceivable.
rows.anchor: nazım yalnız âhara değil, mütefekkirin kendi kendisine bile tefhîm ve temyîz-i ma‘nâda mühim bir vâsıtadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguished Adam by teaching the names, not merely their meanings; the revelation to the Prophet likewise includes both Quranic wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak meleklere karşı Âdem’e verdiği imtiyâzı sade

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran as revealed to the Prophet is not meaning alone, but both its wording and meaning.
rows.anchor: Peygamberimize münzel olan da Kur’ân’ın yalnız mânası değil, hem nazmı ve hem mânasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book is wholly free of doubt and accusation: no other book’s divine truth and guidance of the straight path is known with equal certainty.
rows.anchor: Hadd-i zâtında her türlü şekten ârî ve her töhmetten müberrâdır. Kitaplar içinde hak kitâbullah olduğu bunun kadar kat‘iyyet ve yakīn ile mâlum olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no doubt in how the Quran was revealed or accusation in its delivery; the Prophet witnessed Gabriel’s revelations and his truthfulness and trustworthiness are established.
rows.anchor: Bunun ne keyfiyyet-i vahy ve inzâlinde bir şüphe ne de teblîğinde bir töhmet vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge rests first on full observation and adequate experience, then on truthful reports and historical testimony where direct experience is impossible, and finally on sound rational inference.
rows.anchor: evvelâ şuhûd-i tâm ve tecribe-i kâfiye, sâniyen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those without direct witnessing or experience, the Quran’s inimitability leaves a lasting path to sound inference, guaranteed by God.
rows.anchor: Şuhûd ve tecribeye eremeyenler için de ilelebed delâlet-i i‘câz ile hüsn-i istidlâl tarîki açıktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who doubt the Quran’s perfection and truth fall into two groups: self-interested, stubborn disbelievers with compounded ignorance, or hypocritical skeptics whose suspicion and moral blindness extinguish insight.
rows.anchor: Bunlar ya cehl-i mürekkebe boyanmış, ağrâz-ı mahsûsalarından başka hiçbir şeye hiss-i iltifâtı kalmamış olan mahtûmu’l-kulûb mu‘ânidîn-i keferedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reyb originally means distress or uncertainty in the self, then commonly came to mean doubt; it also carries suspicion or accusation beyond mere doubt.
rows.anchor: örf-i lügatta bu ıztırâba başlıca bir sebep olan şekk ü şüphe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comprehensive negation removes both intellectual doubt and moral suspicion or accusation, affirming the Book’s perfection on both fronts.
rows.anchor: Burada reyb bütün cinsi ile nefyedilmiş olduğundan reyb-i ilmî ve reyb-i ahlâkî diye tefrik olunabilecek olan şek ve töhmet haysiyetlerinin ikisi de selb edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That is the Book” could be the second predicate of “no doubt in it,” but Elmalılı prefers an independent sentence, most eloquently read as an answer to an implied question.
rows.anchor: ذٰلِكَ,لاَ رَيْبَ ف۪يهِ’nin ikinci haberi olabilirse de bir cümle-i müstakille olması daha muhtâr ve bir suâl-i mukadder mülâhazasıyla bir cümle-i istînâfiye olması ise daha beliğdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The assurance answers the Prophet’s imagined concern that humanity might accuse him of composing the Quran himself and falsely attributing it to God; it certifies both Quran and messenger as beyond suspicion.
rows.anchor: Cenâb-ı Allah böyle bir suâle meydan bırakmamak için “bu babda hiçbir vechile irtiyâba mahal yoktur” diye sarâhaten te’mînât-ı mutlaka bahşetmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says the Quran will argue these points in detail through its challenge to doubters and its condemnation of falsely claiming revelation.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bu noktaları ber-tafsil müdafaa ve isbat edecektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This opening addresses epistemology: clear revelation ends philosophical dispute over certainty, reflecting creed’s affirmation that realities are established and knowable and its refutation of skeptical sophists.
rows.anchor: ve “sofestâiyye” denilen ehl-i reyb ve ‘inâdın reddi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even as sciences advance, theoretical and moral skepticism periodically spreads, showing that doubt remains a central problem for humanity.
rows.anchor: ulûm ve fünûnun terakkiyâtına rağmen âlemde gerek nazarî ve gerek ahlâkî reybîliğin vakit vakit tevessü‘etmekte olduğu dahi inkâr olunamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran identifies doubt as humanity’s greatest intellectual and moral heart-disease, then progressively explains the straight path, certainty about unseen and seen realities, God's unity, and ethical practice; al-Baqara’s opening is a general preface to the Quran after al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Bakara’nın başı Fâtiha’dan sonra bütün Kur’ân’ın bir dîbâce-i umûmiyesi demek olduğundan tertîb-i süverin ne kadar tabîî ve ne kadar ilmî ve derin esbâbı ihtivâ ettiği tezahür edeceği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing these teachings with the Prophet’s human surroundings makes it necessarily clear that the Quran is purely divine revelation.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’in muhît-i beşerîsi ile bu hakāik-i ilmiye teemmül ve mukayese edildiği zaman da Kur’ân’ın mücerred vahy-i ilâhî olduğunda zerre kadar iştibâha mahal olmadığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is guidance itself for the God-fearing: proof that teaches right rulings and shows the straight path to those able to leave error and enter God's protection.
rows.anchor: müttakīlere ‘ayn-ı hidâyettir. Dalâletten çıkıp vikāye-i hakka girmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In essence the Book guides all humanity, as 2:185 says; its gracious direction and invitation are universal, but actual attainment is granted to those who have or will acquire taqwā.
rows.anchor: Gerçi bu kitap esas itibariyle هُدًی لِلنَّاسِ’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who have lost their innate capacity will not benefit from guidance and may instead face loss, as 17:82 describes the Quran as healing and mercy for believers but increasing wrongdoers in loss.
rows.anchor: kābiliyyet-i fıtriyelerini zâyi‘etmiş olanlar bundan müstefid olamayacak
